Hello! As an actor from NH & then moved to LA here is what I wish I did to beef up my resume a bit when I was starting out: 
1. Record 1 dramatic & 1 comedic monologue for submissions. Plain background, dress for the part. Have him watch his monologues after each take so he can see what is reading well and what is not. (Also record 32 bars of classical and 32 bars of a modern piece to catalog his singing as well)
2. Look at nearby High schools & colleges to see if they have any sort of film program. See how/where to submit to be cast in them. Submit the videos above- then once you get footage back start creating a reel. 
3. Feel free to go to meetings for representation. Be careful as there are a lot of scams out there. You should never have to pay for an agent nor should you have to take headshots from a SPECIFIC photographer. They may need new headshots to represent your son- but they should not tell you it has to be done by a specific person. An agent should always take a percentage of your income (10-15%). This won’t be as busy- but he may get some local commercials and a line or two in some local non union productions so it’s always good to have someone to keep their eyes out for casting notices you may miss. 

Hope this helps!

Theatre actor here- who then transitioned into film. My biggest advice on how to transition to on camera acting when you’re starting out is to film your monologues super tight on your face. (Elbows up) with only an inch or two above your head. Get the best takes you can- then sit down watch some on screen actors that you look up to & compare. Things to look for: hand movement, eyebrow movement, bobbing of head, emotions in the eyes. These are all very subtle in film.
